uncertain: The renders draw white walls on a white background, so no wall edge is directly visible. Wall ends were fixed from the gable-parapet strips beside the roof, the downpipes, the plinth strip and the drawn gable lines, and checked against the plan: with them every opening lands within about 0.1 m of its plan position. Wall-end error may reach 4-5 px (0.1 m).

The living-room glazing is one corner glazing: B3 on the rear (two panels, counted as one opening because the plan draws one continuous opening with a mullion; two would be possible) and L1 on the left wall.
F1 reaches the floor and is drawn as a sliding unit on the plan, so it is GLAZED_DOOR; WINDOW would be possible. B2 is a narrow floor-reaching glazed door.
Roof windows (two on each slope) light the truss space above the full upper storey, where the section shows no room; they are given level 2.
F2: the box is the door itself; the recess mouth in the wall plane is larger (x 173-245, y 288-387).
The page prints no garage ridge level; by scale the garage gable apex (RIGHT row 159) is about 5.3 m above zero.
Timber panels beside F1, B2 and L1 are cladding or parked sliding shutters, not openings. No chimney is drawn on any elevation.
The page names the side elevations (lewa / prawa) and the plan agrees (corner glazing and kitchen slot window on the left wall, blank garage side on the right). Neither is mirrored.
